e: Over 300 staff affiliated with the Workers First Union at The Warehouse Group's distribution centres in Auckland and Christchurch commence strike action to protest against the use of surveillance artificial intelligence and over job security.
DarkSky International designates Fiordland National Park as the largest international Dark Sky Park in the Southern Hemisphere.
A fast-track approvals panel approves plans to build the Southern Link inland port near Mosgiel.
Police charge a 33-year old man and 28-year old woman with perverting the course of justice in relation to the 2023 death of "Baby Ru."
Academic members of the Tertiary Education Union at the University of Canterbury launch a partial strike by withholding releasing student grades during a pay dispute with the University.
Public broadcaster Radio New Zealand proposes slashing 58 jobs by March 2027 after reporting a record NZ$11.8 million deficit.
Police confirm an arrest has been made in relation to a long-running investigation into the Baby Ru homicide case, which occurred on 22 October 2023.
Forty-three pilot whales die during a mass stranding along the Ngawi coast in the south-eastern North Island.
The unemployment rate rises to 5.7%, marking an 11-year high. About 4,000 jobs are lost in the last quarter.
The New Zealand government ends welfare assistance to 18- and 19-year olds whose parents earn over NZ$67,225.
New Warrant of Fitness regulations extending registration renewals for one year to two years for new vehicles come into force.

The Government announces that it will invest $3.4 million for a 12-month trial to restore Mainlander passenger rail services to Christchurch and establish more frequent train services between Christchurch, Dunedin and Invercargill.
The Waitangi Tribunal finds that the New Zealand Crown breached the Treaty of Waitangi by stripping school boards of their Treaty obligations.

The Dunedin City Council votes by a majority to hold a referendum on whether to retain the Single Transferrable Vote (STV) voting system or to revert to the First Past the Post (FPTP) system during the 2028 New Zealand local elections.

The Otago Regional Council launches a review of a controversial consent granted by the Queenstown Lakes District Council for contractor SJ Allen Holdings to dump treated human waste from Wanaka on farmland near Lauder.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand retains the official cash rate at 2.75% following a split 4–3 vote by the Monetary Policy Council.
The Chief of Defence Force, Air Marshal Tony Davies, resigns after admitting to engaging in an "inappropriate relationship" while in a command role.
Fire and Emergency New Zealand chief executive Kerry Gregory resigns after Minister of Internal Affairs Brooke van Velden declined to express confidence in his leadership.
The National Library of New Zealand and Archives New Zealand confirm plans to lay off 45 jobs as part of a restructuring process, amounting to 11 percent of their workforce.
The High Court rules that the Government's 2025 regulations banning new puberty blocker prescriptions prescriptions for children and young people with gender dysphoria were unlawful.
Over 8,000 university and polytechnic workers affiliated with the Tertiary Education Union go on strike to protest pay conditions and job security.
The New Zealand–India Free Trade Agreement comes into effect.
Spark New Zealand confirms plans to remove all remaining public phone booths over the next two years, citing a lack of "commercial viability."

New Zealand joins Paraguay in abstaining from a non-binding vote at the United Nations General Assembly supporting global pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, citing a need to test the resolution against a "national interest test."
Pakaraka School becomes the first state school in New Zealand to convert to a charter school.
Police find the body of Braydon Hepworth in Hereford Street, Christchurch, where he had been missing since 3 September.

The New Zealand Crown decides not to seek a retrial against David Tamihere, whose convictions for the Murder of Urban Höglin and Heidi Paakkonen were quashed by the Supreme Court of New Zealand in February 2026.
A large wildfire breaks out on the southern shores of Lake Wakatipu in the early hours of the morning, fanned by strong winds.
The New Zealand Government and local government bodies sign the Otago Central Lakes Deal, a ten-year plan to improve infrastructure and healthcare in Central Otago.
Name suppression is lifted for Private Jack Captein, the former New Zealand Army soldier who was convicted in August 2025 of attempted espionage.

A pod of pygmy killer whales become stranded on Ninety Mile Beach in the Far North District. By the following day, at least 12 to 15 whales have died despite efforts by volunteers, iwi and conservation staff to refloat them.

The Greater Wellington Regional Council files criminal charges against both the Wellington City Council and water services provider Tiaki Wai over their handling of the Moa Point wastewater spillage in February 2026.
The 54th New Zealand Parliament is formally dissolved.

Four new road rules allowing children to ride bicycles on footpaths, e-scooters to use cycle lanes, requiring drivers to give way to buses exiting bus stops, and motorists to give cyclists, horse riders and other road users a 1.5 metre passing gap come into effect.

Dutch environmentalist group Both ENDS files a complaint against New Zealand with the European Commission for allegedly breaching the climate change provisions of the EU–NZ free trade agreement. The group's complaint was supported by several New Zealand groups and individuals including Greenpeace New Zealand, the Environmental Law Initiative, Mike Smith and University of Auckland law Professor Jane Kelsey.
Woolworths New Zealand confirms plans to cut 130 customer care jobs in Auckland in order to centralise customer care operations in Sydney.
The Auckland Council votes to shift from postal voting to in-person voting at the 2028 New Zealand local elections.
The Waitangi Tribunal finds that the New Zealand Crown had failed to develop an alternative Māori health plan after it dissolved Te Aka Whai Ora (the Māori Health Authority) in late February 2024.
The Government pauses making decisions on its local government reforms until after the 2026 New Zealand general election.
A fast-track approvals panel rejects mining company Bathurst Resources's application to mine Denniston Plateau on the West Coast Region.
